case_content.title: Case Metadata
case_content.content:
Industry: Technology
Quantitative Level: Easy
Qualitative Level: Medium

case_content.title: Prompt #1 - Canoodle Turnaround
case_content.content: Your client is Canoodle, a revolutionary mobile dating service which utilizes swipe technology allowing users to easily select mates based on their online profiles. Canoodle was started 2 years ago and now operates across the United States. Despite its success and mass popularity, Canoodle has remained unprofitable, and investors are starting to put pressure on the CEO, Stevie McDreamy, to turn the business around. McDreamy has come to you to help out Canoodle. What should they do?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #1
case_content.content:
Provide only upon request:
- Canoodle only operates within the United States with ambitions to expand internationally.
- The app is free to download off all mobile application stores. Canoodle's main source of revenue so far has been through ad sales.
- The company must show a profit within 2 years.
- Canoodle is already an LGBT friendly dating app and caters to the sexual orientation of all its users.
- The market for dating applications consists of approximately 4 major national competitors. Most users typically have 1-3 dating apps, and all 4 competitors have roughly the same number of users within the United States.
- Canoodle does not consider traditional online dating websites in the same market.

case_content.title: Exhibit #1 - Canoodle's Previous Performance
case_content.content:
Exhibit #1: Canoodle's Previous Performance

Metrics shown:
- Revenue ($000's)
- User Base (000's)
- Total Expenses ($000's)

Time periods shown:
- 1QFY2014

- 3QFY2014
- 4QFY2014
- 1QFY2015
- 2QFY2015
- 3QFY2015
- 4QFY2015

The chart ranges from 0 to 1,500.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Exhibit #1
case_content.content:
The interviewee should pick up on the fact that revenues have fallen with the slower growth in the user base. Additionally, costs have stabilized. This is a revenue problem.

Ask the candidate to brainstorm sources of revenue.

Possible revenue sources:
- Selling user demographic data, with risk of potential privacy issues.
- Selling outside services, such as emojis or stickers.
- Selling a premium upgrade to users.
- Charging on the application store.

case_content.title: Prompt #2 - Premium Service Investment
case_content.content: Upon hearing your suggestions, McDreamy is inclined to pursue a “premium” service for consumers to use. The development team estimates costs at $500,000 and would take 6 months to develop. What factors should McDreamy consider before committing to the investment?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #2
case_content.content:
The candidate should pick up on difficulties entering a new market:
- Price.
- Market size.
- Adoption rate.
- Marketing.

Bonus points if they identify:
- Customer churn or impacts on the current customer base.
- Transaction costs.
- Implementation timeline and competitive response.

case_content.title: Prompt #3 - CanoodlePremium City Launch
case_content.content: Due to staff and server capacity issues, McDreamy has decided that he would like to launch in just one city this year before rolling out nationwide. Which city would be the best for CanoodlePremium to launch in?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #3
case_content.content:
Provide the candidate with the exhibit. If the candidate asks, the price for the premium service per month is $3. The candidate should know to ask what the price per month would be.

McDreamy wants the initiative to breakeven within 6 months of launching.

case_content.content:
City | User base (thousands of users) | Adoption rate
New York | 300 | 9%

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Exhibit #2
case_content.content:
Exhibit #2 Guidance:

City | User base (thousands of users) | Adoption rate | 6-month revenue
New York | 300 | 9% | $486.00
Los Angeles | 350 | 8% | $504.00
Chicago | 200 | 10% | $360.00
Houston | 175 | 9% | $283.50
Washington D.C. | 230 | 7% | $289.80

Analysis:
- Los Angeles is the only city that breaks even in 6 months.

case_content.title: Final Recommendation
case_content.content: Canoodle should launch a premium service in Los Angeles.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Final Recommendation
case_content.content:
Concerns:
- Sensitivity around adoption rate.
- Risk of launching in one city versus all at once.
- Extra maintenance costs for premium service.
- Competitive response.

Next Steps:
- Development, either in house or contracted.
